newsitem.title: GERMANY: Stark - knows of no plans to keep Italy out of EMU.
newsitem.headline: Stark - knows of no plans to keep Italy out of EMU.

text.p: A senior German finance ministry official said on Tuesday that he knew of no plans aimed at trying to keep Italy out of the first group of nations to participate in the planned single European currency.

"There are no such plans, at least if there is work being done on such a plan it is not being done with Germany's participation," Juergen Stark, state secretary in the finance ministry, said at a banking forum.
Stark made had been asked to comment on reports that German officials were eager to prevent Italy from entering monetary union at its scheduled start in January 1999.
"I cannot say who will qualify," Stark said. "Of course, we are interested in having as many nations as possible join the currency union."
Stark also acknowledged that Germany still had a way to go in meeting the entry criteria for currency union laid out in the Maastricht Treaty.
"We still have to do our homework," Stark said.
